title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026 · Gambler edition · By Richie Diskin

paragraphs: Monday night is final, so all 14 Week 8 games are graded, from Thursday night in Green Bay to Monday night in Seattle. The last sweat of the week went the wrong way early for most of the room, came back to life for about three minutes in the fourth quarter, and then got buried by a 39-yard run and three D'Andre Swift touchdowns.

Graded against the opening lines, the Cover Writer went 6-8 against the spread and 5-9 on the over/under. Graded against the closing lines, the Cover Writer went 6-8 against the spread and 8-6 on the over/under.

Every side is graded on the team picked and every over/under on the Over or Under called, once against the opening line and once against the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss, overtime points count, and a pick pulled before kickoff is not graded. Monday night gets the full ride. The rest of the week gets a quick lap, with the plays that swung the tickets.

Opening line: Seahawks −4.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Seahawks −3.5, over/under 46.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Seahawks −3 and the Under 46.5, projecting Seahawks 25, Bears 19. Final: Bears 34, Seahawks 17. The Bears won by 17, and the teams scored 51 points.

Everybody holding a ticket on this one was on the Under. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch laid the points with Seattle, Next Man Up took the Bears, and Follow The Money had no pick. In The Trenches had the Bears and the Under on its card until Monday morning, then pulled both when Seattle ruled left tackle Charles Cross out. So the Seattle crowd needed a win by 4 at the closing number and by 5 at the opener, and the Under crowd needed 46 points or fewer at the close and 47 or fewer at the open.

The Seattle tickets were in trouble before the Seahawks ever touched the ball in Chicago territory. The Bears opened with a 17-play, 80-yard drive that ate 8:32, kept alive by Colston Loveland's 15-yard catch on 3rd-and-1, and Caleb Williams hit Luther Burden III from 1 yard out at 5:25 of the first. Jason Myers got Seattle on the board with a 27-yarder at 12:50 of the second, and Cairo Santos answered from 44 and 38. Bears 13, Seahawks 3, with 1:08 left in the half. Under tickets were sitting pretty at 16 points.

Then the last minute of the half. A 16-yard interference flag on Jaylon Johnson kept Seattle moving, and on 3rd-and-10 Sam Darnold hit Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 43-yard touchdown with 30 seconds left. Myers pushed the extra point wide left. Bears 13, Seahawks 9 at the half, 22 points. Seattle backers were 4 points down and needed to win the second half by 8 at the close and 9 at the open. The Under had 24 points of room at the close and 25 at the open.

Chicago went three-and-out to start the third, and Montez Sweat sacked Darnold on Seattle's next series. Then the Bears went 69 yards in 10 plays, and Swift scored from 1 yard out at 5:38. Bears 20, Seahawks 9, 29 points, and Seahawks −3.5 was now 14.5 points on the wrong side.

The next drive is the one Seattle backers will be replaying all week. George Holani returned the kickoff 34 yards to the Seattle 41. A defensive holding flag on Kyler Gordon wiped out a Sweat sack. Tory Horton caught a 13-yarder to the Chicago 13. Then, on 2nd-and-8 from the 11 with 14 seconds left in the third, Darnold found Smith-Njigba down at the Chicago 1, and the flag came out on Smith-Njigba for offensive interference. Back to the 21. One incompletion, confirmed by replay, and a 6-yard catch by Zach Charbonnet later, Myers lined up a 33-yarder on 4th-and-12, and Austin Booker blocked it. Instead of first-and-goal at the 1, Seattle came away with nothing, and the Under crowd got a free 3 points of breathing room.

Seattle got the ball right back. Mike Morris sacked Williams for 10, and on 3rd-and-20 DeMarcus Lawrence punched the ball loose from Loveland and recovered it at the Chicago 25. Cam Lewis picked off Darnold in the end zone two snaps later, and a defensive holding flag on Chicago wiped it out. Darnold hit Cooper Kupp for a 7-yard touchdown at 11:46, then hit Horton for the two-point try. Bears 20, Seahawks 17, 37 points, and now everybody was sweating. The Seattle crowd needed to outscore Chicago by 7 the rest of the way at the close and by 8 at the open. The Under had 9 points of room at the close and 10 at the open, with 11:46 to play.

That room lasted 3:18. Zavion Thomas returned the kickoff 24 yards and Morris got flagged 15 more for unnecessary roughness. Chicago took a delay of game on third down, turning it into 3rd-and-9 at the Seattle 44, and Kalif Raymond ran 39 yards to the Seattle 5. Swift scored on the next snap at 8:28. Bears 27, Seahawks 17, 44 points. The side was gone. At the closing 46.5, any field goal now killed the Under. At the opening 47.5, the Under could survive a field goal but not a touchdown.

The Under at the open still had one prayer: keep Chicago out of the end zone. Seattle's Irv Charles got flagged for unnecessary roughness on the kickoff return, a holding flag on Tyrique Stevenson Sr. wiped out another Sweat sack, and on 3rd-and-7 James Lynch picked off Darnold and returned it 16 yards to the Seattle 6 at 6:01. Under backers needed a goal-line stand. They got an unnecessary roughness flag on Seattle's Nick Emmanwori instead, and even a Chicago delay of game from the 1 only backed the Bears up to the 5. Swift scored from there at 4:41, his third touchdown. Bears 34, Seahawks 17, 51 points. The Under was dead at both numbers.

Seattle's last drive got to the Chicago 7 behind a roughing the passer flag on Booker and a 14-yard Darnold scramble, and 4th-and-4 fell incomplete to Kupp at 2:21. Williams knelt it out. Swift finished with 27 carries for 69 yards and 3 touchdowns. Smith-Njigba caught 6 for 118 yards and the touchdown, and Seattle went 1 for 11 on third down and 1 for 4 in the red zone.

The damage report. The Seahawks lost by 17, so laying 4.5 at the open missed by 21.5 and laying 3.5 at the close missed by 20.5. The Cover Writer projected Seahawks 25, Bears 19, and the Bears scored 34 by themselves. The Formula had Seahawks 28, Bears 16, Seattle by 12, and got Chicago by 17, a 29-point miss on the margin. Letdown Watch had Seahawks 25, Bears 20. Next Man Up, projecting Seahawks 23, Bears 22, was the only Bears backer in the room and cashed the side by 21.5 at the open and 20.5 at the close, then gave one right back on the Under. In The Trenches pulled a Bears +3 that would have covered by 20 and an Under 46.5 that would have gone over by 4.5, so the Cross scratch cost it one winner and saved it one loser. Follow The Money watched from the couch.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Seahawks, missed by 21.5 points at the opening Seahawks −4.5 and missed by 20.5 points at the closing Seahawks −3.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 3.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 4.5 points at the closing 46.5.
Called it at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Bears, covered by 21.5 points at the opening Bears +4.5 and covered by 20.5 points at the closing Bears +3.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the over/under; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Opening line: Packers −7, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Packers −3.5, over/under 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Panthers and the Under, projecting Panthers 22, Packers 24. Final: Panthers 19, Packers 27. The Packers won by 8, and the teams scored 46 points.

Thursday night set the tone. Green Bay led 27-10 after Love's 4-yard touchdown to Josh Jacobs at 7:30 of the third, and Trey Smack's first extra point had already hit the left upright. Bryce Young hit Jalen Coker for 26 yards at 5:37 of the fourth, the two-point try failed, and the scoreboard froze at 46 points. The Under cashed at the closing 47.5 and lost at the opening 45.5 by half a point. One more missed kick, by either team, and the opening Under cashes.
Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Panthers, missed by 1 point at the opening Panthers +7 and missed by 4.5 points at the closing Panthers +3.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by half a point at the opening 45.5 and stayed under by 1.5 points at the closing 47.5; The Formula on the Over, went over by half a point at the opening 45.5 and fell short by 1.5 points at the closing 47.5.
Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Packers, covered by 1 point at the opening Packers −7 and covered by 4.5 points at the closing Packers −3.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the over/under; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

Half a point, both ways. Murray hit T.J. Hockenson for an 8-yard touchdown at 8:44 of the fourth and Jordan Addison caught the two-point throw, 15-12 Vikings. Arizona had the points at every number and won the game outright, so the side was never the sweat. The Under was. Brandon Aubrey's 41-yarder at 1:09 made it 30-24, 54 points on the board, half a point under the closing 54.5. Minshew hit Michael Wilson for the tying touchdown with 6 seconds left, and Chad Ryland's 42-yarder won it in overtime.

Opening line: Jets −1.5, over/under 40.5. Closing line: Jets −1.5, over/under 46.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Jets and the Under, projecting Raiders 21, Jets 24. Final: Raiders 38, Jets 33. The Raiders won by 5, and the teams scored 71 points.

An unnecessary roughness flag on Jeremy Chinn handed New York 15 free yards, and on the next snap Chinn picked off Geno Smith in the end zone.

The side was over at halftime, 28-0. The over/under was the sweat. On the last play of the third, Lawrence hit Bhayshul Tuten for a 25-yard touchdown, 42-7, 49 points, and nobody scored in the fourth. The Over cashed at the closing 45.5 and lost at the opening 49.5 by half a point.

A Derrick Henry touchdown run in the third came back on a holding call, Baltimore settled for a field goal, and the Ravens never scored again. Allen added touchdowns to DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid in the fourth, and the 46 points stayed under the opening 51.5 and the closing 55.

Cleveland never saw the end zone. Andre Szmyt's two field goals were all the Browns got, Pat Freiermuth took a direct snap in from 1 yard with a second left in the half, and the Over needed 40 at the open and 39 at the close and stopped at 33.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Browns, missed by 15 points at the opening Browns +6 and missed by 17.5 points at the closing Browns +3.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 6.5 points at the opening 39.5 and fell short by 5.5 points at the closing 38.5.

Atlanta got shut out. Alex Anzalone intercepted Penix twice in the first quarter, Zyon McCollum added one in the fourth, and the Under cashed by 30.5 at the open and 27 at the close.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Falcons, missed by 11.5 points at the opening Falcons +4.5 and missed by 14 points at the closing Falcons +2; The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over, fell short by 30.5 points at the opening 46.5 and fell short by 27 points at the closing 43.

Opening line: Broncos −1.5, over/under 43.5. Closing line: Broncos +0.5, over/under 42. The Cover Writer's card had the Broncos and the Over, projecting Chiefs 22, Broncos 21. Final: Chiefs 24, Broncos 28. The Broncos won by 4, and the teams scored 52 points.

Nix's 2-yard touchdown to Nate Adkins and Waddle's two-point catch at 8:55 of the fourth put 45 points on the board and cashed the Over at both numbers. Jonah Coleman scored from 5 at 1:56, and then the Chiefs got to the Denver 1. Walker got stuffed, a flag for moving early backed Kansas City up to the 6, and Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes at the 12 as the clock ran out.

Missed at both numbers: The Formula on the Chiefs, missed by 2.5 points at the opening Chiefs +1.5 and missed by 4.5 points at the closing Chiefs −0.5; Follow The Money on the Under, went over by 8.5 points at the opening 43.5 and went over by 10 points at the closing 42.

Same 43 points, two different tickets. Willis threw a 35-yard touchdown to K. Coleman with 2:04 left to get the Dolphins covering, and the two-point throw fell incomplete. The Over came up 2.5 short at the opening 45.5 and cashed at the closing 41.5 by a point and a half.
Missed at both numbers: The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Patriots, missed by 2 points at the opening Patriots −7 and missed by 2 points at the closing Patriots −7.

Opening line: Rams −4.5, over/under 48.5. Closing line: Rams −6.5, over/under 45.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Rams and the Under, projecting Chargers 18, Rams 26. Final: Chargers 9, Rams 24. The Rams won by 15, and the teams scored 33 points.

The Chargers led 9-3 on three Cameron Dicker field goals, and then the Rams took over. Kyren Williams scored with 19 seconds left in the half, Blake Corum ran 23 yards for a touchdown in the third, and Stafford hit Puka Nacua for 18 yards after Trent McDuffie intercepted Justin Herbert.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Chargers, missed by 10.5 points at the opening Chargers +4.5 and missed by 8.5 points at the closing Chargers +6.5; Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Over, fell short by 15.5 points at the opening 48.5 and fell short by 12.5 points at the closing 45.5.

No pick: Follow The Money on the side.

Opening line: Eagles −1.5, over/under 46.5. Closing line: Commanders −5.5, over/under 40.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Eagles and the Over, projecting Commanders 24, Eagles 21. Final: Eagles 10, Commanders 27. The Commanders won by 17, and the teams scored 37 points.

The Eagles led 10-0 and never scored again. Jake Elliott's 36-yarder came off the board on an illegal formation flag, and from 41 yards he hit the left upright at 9:01 of the fourth. On the last snap, McKee hit Eli Stowers for 34 yards to the Washington 8 as time ran out, and the Over at the closing 40.5 died 8 yards from the end zone.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Eagles, missed by 18.5 points at the opening Eagles −1.5 and missed by 11.5 points at the closing Eagles +5.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over, fell short by 9.5 points at the opening 46.5 and fell short by 3.5 points at the closing 40.5.
Called it at both numbers: Follow The Money on the Commanders, covered by 18.5 points at the opening Commanders +1.5 and covered by 11.5 points at the closing Commanders −5.5.
No pick: Follow The Money on the over/under; In The Trenches on the side or the over/under.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: Week 8 is closed. The Cover Writer missed 17 times and hit 11 times at the opening lines, and missed 14 times and hit 14 times at the closing lines.

The Cover Writer finished Week 8 at 6-8 against the spread at both numbers, and 5-9 on the over/under at the open and 8-6 at the close. Monday night took one off each column. It asked for one game this week that a kicker did not decide, got exactly that, and lost by 20.5 anyway. Week 9 is a clean slate, and the Cover Writer plans to treat it like one.

The Formula finished Week 8 at 3-11 against the spread at the open and 5-9 at the close, and 7-7 on the over/under at the open and 4-10 at the close. It said Monday night would put it back in the conversation or send it into hiding. Seahawks by 12 turned into Bears by 17, so check under the desk. The Bears are home Sunday night against the Buccaneers, and The Formula might want to think twice before fading them again.

Next Man Up finished Week 8 at 6-8 against the spread at both numbers, and 5-9 on the over/under at the open and 8-6 at the close. It was the only one in the room on Chicago, it cashed by 20.5 at the close, and it will be bringing that up until Thursday's kickoff. It also had the Under on Monday night, so maybe not too loudly.

Letdown Watch finished Week 8 at 10-4 against the spread at the open and 8-6 at the close, and 5-9 on the over/under at the open and 4-10 at the close. That is the best side record in the room at the open. The over/under is the anchor around its ankle, and Monday night added one more to the wrong column. It spent all week hunting letdowns and then laid the points with the team that had one.

Follow The Money finished Week 8 at 2-0 against the spread at both numbers, and 1-3 on the over/under at both numbers. Two side picks all week, two winners, and a Monday night on the couch. It will tell you it saw the Bears coming. It did not pick them.

In The Trenches finished Week 8 at 6-5 against the spread at both numbers, and 7-4 on the over/under at the open and 9-2 at the close. It sat out Sunday night and Monday night. The Monday scratch was a wash, one winner and one loser left on the table, and that over/under record at the close is the best anybody in the room put up this week. The rest of the panel can say whatever it wants about the bench time.

Next week starts Thursday at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video with the Jaguars at the Ravens. The Bears, now 6-2, are home Sunday night against the Buccaneers at 8:20 PM ET on NBC, and the three pickers who laid points against them in Seattle have four days to decide whether they want another piece. The Seahawks, now 4-4, host the Cardinals at 4:25 PM ET Sunday on Fox, and Seattle backers would settle for a kicker who gets every one through. Week 9 closes Monday night with the Bills at the Vikings.
